title: Mo and the Sleepy Little Dinosaur

beats.chapter: Mo and the Sleepy Little Dinosaur
beats.text: Mo and the Sleepy Little Dinosaur
Tonight, {child|little one}, Mo is flying a long, long way back in time. To a land of giant ferns and sleepy dinosaurs.
Stomp... stomp... stomp. Look, a little dinosaur with a long, long neck, and a long, long tail.
It is yawning a big dinosaur yawn. It wants to go to bed, but it has lost the way to its cosy cave.
Mo has an idea. We can help the little dinosaur find its way home.
Make a crocodile: two flat hands, one on top of the other, like a long snappy mouth.
A crocodile! Crocodiles lived with the dinosaurs, long ago. They are very old cousins. Climb on, Mo.
Swim across the warm, muddy swamp. Splish, splash. The little dinosaur stomps along behind.
The crocodile slides back into the water, and blows a sleepy bubble.
Now the path splits in two. Which way is home? Look closely at the stones.
Make a snail: a fist for the shell, and two fingers poking forward for its eyes.
A snail! Its shell has a spiral, just like the old stone shells hidden in these rocks. They are called fossils.
Slowly, slowly, follow the fossils along the stony path.
The snail found the right path. It tucks itself into its shell, for a little sleep.
The ferns are very tall here. Too tall to see over. Who can fly up high and look?
Make a bird with two hands, side by side. Fly up high above the ferns.
A bird! Here is a secret: birds are the great, great grandchildren of the dinosaurs.
Up, up, over the ferns. Look, there is the cave, just over there.
The bird flaps its wings, and the little dinosaur stomps after it, stomp, stomp.
But the cave is very dark inside, and the little dinosaur is a tiny bit scared.
Look! A little firefly, glowing softly. It wants to help too.
Cup your hands together, softly, and carry the firefly to the cave.
You have it. Hold it close, so its light is warm and gentle.
Now open your hands, and let the firefly light up the cave.
The cave glows, warm and golden, and there is the little dinosaur's nest.
The little dinosaur stomps inside, curls its long tail round, and closes its eyes. Safe and snug.
Goodnight, little dinosaur. Goodnight, sleepy volcano. And goodnight, {child|little one}. Mo will see you tomorrow.
The End
The End
